# Remove Digit From Number to Maximize Result.

@example Erasing the first 7 leaves 437, and erasing the second leaves 473.
"4737"
"7"
=> "473"

@example Erasing the first 2 brings the 8 to the front; erasing the second leaves 2883.
"28283"
"2"
=> "8283"

@example Every choice leaves 777.
"7777"
"7"
=> "777"

# The smallest input; the only copy is first.
"12"
"1"
=> "2"

# A 9 is never followed by a larger digit, so the last 9 is erased.
"91929"
"9"
=> "9192"

# The first copy is followed by a smaller digit, the second by a larger one.
"4246"
"4"
=> "426"

# The first copy is followed by a larger digit; erasing the last is worse.
"3837"
"3"
=> "837"

# A run of copies followed by a smaller digit, then a copy followed by a
# larger one: erasing inside the run is worse.
"66568"
"6"
=> "6658"

# A run of copies followed by a smaller digit, then a copy at the end.
"7737"
"7"
=> "773"

# No copy is followed by a larger digit, and smaller digits lie between
# the copies: the last copy is erased.
"8381"
"8"
=> "831"

# digit is 1.
"1121"
"1"
=> "121"

# The only copy is the last digit.
"98765"
"5"
=> "9876"

# 100 digits. The two candidates first differ at their 31st digit, beyond
# what any integer type or a double can tell apart; the first copy wins.
"9999999999999999999999999999994577777777777777777777436666666666666666666666666666666666666666666666"
"4"
=> "999999999999999999999999999999577777777777777777777436666666666666666666666666666666666666666666666"

# 100 digits. The candidates first differ at their 51st digit; the last
# copy wins.
"1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111121111111111111111111121111111111111111111111111111"
"2"
=> "111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111112111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111"

# 100 copies of 3.
"3333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333"
"3"
=> "333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333"

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"8787"
"7"
=> "887"

@gen 2 small
"332334"
"3"
=> "33234"

@gen 3 small
"2222212"
"2"
=> "222221"

@gen 4 small
"878"
"8"
=> "87"

@gen 5 small
"88887"
"8"
=> "8887"

@gen 6 small
"12111"
"1"
=> "2111"

@gen 7 small
"66776"
"6"
=> "6776"

# Full-size random cases, 100 digits: digit 9; digits no larger than 2
# except for a 3 near the end; and digits from 1 to 9.
@gen 1
"9999889999899999988899989989998999999999888998999999989998988999988898899999899999899989999989899899"
"9"
=> "999988999989999998889998998999899999999988899899999998999898899998889889999989999989998999998989989"

@gen 3
"2222211221111112112222122222222222211121222222111211212121222122221222121222211211222122211122122311"
"2"
=> "222221122111111211222212222222222221112122222211121121212122212222122212122221121122212221112212311"

@gen 4
"1687582538885288587818862858485738358818888348728828164587188545188888685884888185855887588328978836"
"8"
=> "168758253888528858781886285848573835881888834872882816458718854518888868588488818585588758832978836"
